title: Exact sparse-spectrum learning guarantee
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let the target be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube whose Fourier spectrum has at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero coefficients. For every outcome in the support of the learning program’s cost distribution on this target, the output hypothesis evaluates exactly to the target and has relative Hamming distance zero from it; the outcome uses zero random examples, and both its number of membership queries and its charged local work are at most $1+2^{171}\bigl(12(n+1)(2^k+1)^2\bigr)^{100}$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The target belongs to the exact sparse-spectrum class, meaning its Fourier sparsity is at most $2^{k+1}$
The hypothesis-and-cost outcome lies in the support of the learning program’s cost distribution for that target
